topic: Dark-Agent: Mythic C2 Agent With In-Memory BOF Loader for macOS/Linux

key_points: First open-source Mythic C2 agent with full in-memory BOF (COFF/ELF) loader for Linux x86_64/aarch64 and macOS (arm64 Apple Silicon, x86-64).
Written in Crystal with statically-linked OpenSSL; no libssl dependency on target.
Ships 25 BOFs and 15 built-in commands out of box; minimal offensive capability baked in (just the loader).
BOFs loaded in-memory via BofRegistry — no disk writes, no tmp memfd files, no child processes; BOF runs inside existing agent process.
C2 profiles: HTTP and HTTPX (malleable); AES-256-CBC encryption toggle, domain rotation (round-robin/fail-over), base64/URL transforms, message placement in headers/URL params/cookies/body.
Direct mode: build standalone COFF loader to test BOFs without a Mythic server.
MITRE ATT&CK mappings per command (T1059, T1082, T1070, T1129, T1033, T1016).
Official deep-dive (Part 1): Dark used by ServiceNow Red Team since 2024, operationally proven against modern defenses.

Workflow: bof_load pulls compiled object from Mythic file store over C2 → registers in BofRegistry as raw bytes (nothing mapped to executable memory yet); bof_list shows loaded; bof_exec fires it (runnable repeatedly without re-upload).
Entrypoint is coffee() to stay familiar to operators building BOFs; includes beacon.h boilerplate.
Brought BOF execution to Linux and macOS including Apple Silicon m-series.
Build via ./build.sh -b (Linux) / -B (macOS aarch64, requires Zig + macOS SDK); cross-compiles all four targets in a single Mythic Docker container.
Working jQuery HTTPX profile included (httpx-profile.json); Part 2 forthcoming.
Fawkes: cross-platform Mythic C2 agent (Java) supporting Windows (EXE/DLL/shellcode), Linux (ELF/shared libs), macOS (Mach-O Intel + Apple Silicon).
213 commands total (113 cross-platform, 82 Windows-only, 21 Unix-only, 6 macOS-only).
Inline BOF execution via Forge (inline-execute / coff_arguments / function_name), plus inline-assembly.
Contrast: Fawkes is broader multi-platform but Dark focuses specifically on first-class in-memory BOF on Unix and ships BOFs pre-built.
Kassandra: in-memory execution of BOFs, .NET assemblies, Python in a C2 agent; BOF runs in an isolated subprocess spawned from the agent binary via stdin/stdout JSON.
Chunked download protocol (4096-byte chunks, CHUNK_SIZE) negotiates with Mythic server.
Isolation pattern ensures a crashing BOF doesn't kill the agent (unlike Dark's in-process execution).
Contrast: Dark executes in-process (no fork/subprocess, lower footprint) vs Kassandra's crash-isolation.
Woopsie: cross-platform Mythic C2 agent in Java (JAR + GraalVM Native Image), works on Windows/Linux/macOS.
C2 profiles HTTP, HTTPX, WebSocket.
coff_loader command executes BOFs on Windows only.
Contrast: Woopsie's BOF support is Windows-only; Dark is the Unix/macOS-first BOF loader.

stats.fact: Dark is the first open-source Mythic C2 agent with a full in-memory BOF loader for macOS (including Apple Silicon) and Linux.
Dark ships out of the box with 25 BOFs and 15 built-in commands.
Dark has been used operationally by the ServiceNow Red Team since 2024.
GitHub repo created 2026-08-12; ~100 stars, 13 forks at write time.
Mythic framework v4.0.0 supports Dark-Agent in the mythicmeta community overview.
Cross-compiles four targets in one Mythic Docker container: macOS arm64, macOS x86-64, Linux arm64, Linux x86-64.
Crystal language enables no-GC-native single binary; static OpenSSL avoids libssl dependency on target Linux.

angles: First Unix-native in-memory BOF loader for Mythic — closes the gap that Poseidon and Windows-only agents left for Linux/macOS operators.
Operationally proven: used by ServiceNow Red Team since 2024 (long before public open-source release), not a hobby project.
Stealth design: zero disk writes, no memfd/tmp files, no child processes — BOF executes in-process, minimizing artifact surface.
Lean payload philosophy: ships only a BOF loader, so the initial drop is 'Dark on arrival' with minimal baked-in capability; operators extend with BOFs.
macOS/Apple Silicon support is a standout — most C2 agents ignore macOS, let alone m-series in-memory COFF loading.
Mythic ecosystem fit: supports HTTP + HTTPX malleable profiles, Forge integration for building BOFs, direct/standalone mode for dev testing.
Open-source release timing and ServiceNow's intent to have operators 'break it, open issues, write bad BOFs'.
